lens: mobile task completion, visual hierarchy, accessibility, and recovery

findings.observation: The 390-pixel structural prototype demonstrates an Agent-first viewport and direct transition to the person page, and the production CSS contains explicit 840- and 640-pixel fallbacks. The authenticated production build was not successfully exercised at a real 390-pixel browser viewport in this review.
findings.evidence: workspace-concept-a-mobile-chat.png and workspace-concept-a-mobile-page.png; apps/web/app/globals.css media queries at max-width 840px and 640px; desktop executable build only for the final production artifact.
findings.user_impact: The intended mobile hierarchy is plausible, but clipping, keyboard avoidance, nested scrolling, browser chrome, and real touch behavior remain unproven.
findings.recommendation: Run the production flow on a small and large iPhone viewport and an iOS Simulator, including create contact, add source, ask Agent, open People, review a long fact, background, and resume.
findings.verification: At 390 pixels and on the smallest supported iPhone, complete the full task with no horizontal overflow, hidden primary action, nested-scroll trap, keyboard obstruction, or loss after interruption.

findings.observation: The production mobile shell now uses a 64-pixel bottom bar, 44-pixel primary targets, visible Agent, People, and Sources labels, and a 44-pixel Agent composer action. The final rendered mobile surface has not been visually inspected after this correction.
findings.evidence: apps/web/app/globals.css sets the bottom navigation and Agent actions to at least 44 pixels below 840 and 640 pixels; mobile prototype screenshots show the intended bottom-navigation composition.
findings.user_impact: The code meets the minimum target geometry, but content expansion or safe-area insets may still compress labels or place controls too close to the home indicator.
findings.recommendation: Add safe-area padding, inspect localization expansion, and test labels and targets with touch visualization on real device sizes.
findings.verification: Agent, People, Sources, add-source, theme, and Ask Agent remain distinct and tappable at 200 percent text expansion with bottom safe-area inset applied.

findings.observation: The DOM exposes labeled regions, textboxes, buttons, status announcements, and non-color operation states. Dynamic Type, VoiceOver order, focus return after Agent navigation, reduced motion, dark mode, slow network, and offline recovery were not directly tested for this redesigned shell.
findings.evidence: Browser DOM snapshots expose Relationship Agent, person page, governed source controls, operation status, and live status text; apps/web/app/globals.css includes a reduced-motion rule.
findings.user_impact: A screen-reader or large-text user may encounter a different hierarchy than the visual prototype, and a slow Agent response may leave the small viewport without enough context.
findings.recommendation: Run the mobile review matrix at default, XXXL, AX3, and AX5 with VoiceOver, reduced motion, dark mode, slow network, and app background or foreground transitions.
findings.verification: The critical path is correctly announced in evidence-to-action order, focus lands on the affected object after Agent navigation, progress is honest, and the user can recover without duplicate writes.

strengths: Chat occupies the first mobile viewport without replacing the canonical person page.
The bottom navigation preserves direct access to Agent, People, and Sources with visible labels.
Critical mobile targets are coded at 44 pixels or larger after review.
The interface uses text labels in addition to color for staged, completed, no-change, confirmed, and no-action states.
The layout uses 100dvh-aware sizing and provides reduced-motion behavior.
missing_evidence: Authenticated production build at 390 pixels and on real iPhone sizes.
VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, keyboard, safe-area, localization, and focus-order results.
Slow-network, offline, cancellation, and interruption recovery.
Dark-mode visual inspection of the redesigned workspace.
Real-device evidence for screenshot intake and evidence review.
open_questions: Should mobile return to the last selected Agent or People surface, or always start in Agent for a relationship URL?
Which operation receipt needs to remain visible above the keyboard after a Chat-triggered page action?
